title: Dori: User Centered HPC for Data Intensive Computing
problem: Mixed production/research HPC clusters serving diverse user bases with data-intensive workloads require balancing governance, resource allocation, user support, and software infrastructure. Traditional cluster management approaches insufficient for genomics and bioinformatics scale.
motivation: Joint Genome Institute (JGI) processes petabytes of biological data requiring specialized HPC infrastructure. Mixed production and research workloads create complex governance and resource management challenges.
method: Describes Dori, JGI's primary HPC cluster since 2022, with focus on: (1) governance and communications models addressing mixed workload needs, (2) software tools addressing diverse user requirements, (3) operational lessons from processing petabytes of genomic data.
key_novelty: User-centered design philosophy for data-intensive HPC cluster; integrated governance/communications/tools approach for mixed production-research environments.
contributions: User-centered HPC cluster design and governance
Governance and communications model for diverse stakeholders
Software tools for data-intensive genomics computing
Operational insights from petabyte-scale data processing
limitations: Abstract provides limited technical details on cluster architecture
Specific software tools and innovations not enumerated
Performance metrics and throughput not provided
Scalability to other data-intensive domains unclear
primary_theme: User-Centered HPC Operations for Data-Intensive Science
